title: Snow Day
logline: Michael keeps everyone late for a 'Winter Wellness' seminar until the roads close, trapping half the office overnight; Jim and Pam share a vending-machine dinner, and Dwight and Angela share a survival blanket.
outline: A: Michael delays dismissal for a pointless seminar, strands half the office, and tries to make the night a family sleepover; Kevin's chili saves it, and Michael admits why he wanted them to stay. B: Roy can't get through; Jim and Pam spend a quiet evening with vending-machine dinner and her sketchbook. C: Dwight's survival supplies, and a shared blanket that Kevin almost sees. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, A, C, A, B, A, tag
storySoFar: Michael stalled corporate's noon storm closing with a 'Winter Wellness' seminar until the roads closed, stranding half the office overnight; Bob Vance rescued Phyllis, and Stanley walked out mid-slide. Michael's 'Snow Games' flopped, but Kevin's emergency chili made it a party, and Michael admitted to Oscar that his apartment is too quiet; they played gin rummy. Jim and Pam shared a vending-machine dinner and she told him she wanted to illustrate children's books; at midnight Roy called to say the plow came and he was coming for her. Dwight and Angela shared a survival blanket and Kevin almost noticed. Kelly counts sleeping near Ryan as a milestone. Earlier: Michael ranked last in the manager survey (Angela wrote the harsh comment; Dwight protected her); Pam is taking an art class on Tuesdays; corporate will close Scranton or Stamford; Jan kissed Michael and faxed that it didn't happen.

stateChanges.progress: Snowed in: vending-machine dinner and a quiet night; Roy came for her at midnight
Shared a survival blanket; Kevin saw and asked to get in

stateChanges.status: Gin rummy partners after the snowstorm; Oscar is less angry

Pam wanted to illustrate children's books when she was ten

scenes.recap: Dwight arrives dragging a sled of survival supplies for a storm that hasn't started.

beats.text: 8:30 AM. FORECAST: 14 INCHES

beats.caption: drags in a sled loaded with canned beets, rope and a hand-crank radio

beats.text: Dwight, it's not snowing.
Not YET. The weak prepare when it snows. The strong prepare when it's sunny.
Is that a whole sled of beets?
And one can of peaches. For morale.

scenes.recap: Corporate says close at noon; Michael insists on finishing his 'Winter Wellness' seminar first.

beats.text: Michael, corporate emailed. All branches close at noon because of the storm.
And we will close at noon. Right after my Winter Wellness seminar. Which is very short.
Slide one. 'Snow: Friend or Foe?' Discuss.

beats.caption: puts on his coat and walks out mid-slide

beats.text: Stanley will be marked as 'Foe.'
1:40 PM. STILL ON SLIDE FOUR

lines: The seminar had nine slides. Three of them were the same picture of a snowman.
One of the snowmen was Michael. He'd drawn a tie on it.

scenes.recap: Pam calls Roy; his truck is stuck, the roads are closing, and he can't come.

beats.text: You're stuck? In the ditch? No, I'm fine. Are you fine? Okay. Just... okay.
No Roy?
His truck's in a ditch on Route 6. They're closing the roads. I guess I live here now.
Well, the commute is great.

scenes.recap: Dwight inventories his survival supplies with Angela and gives her the good blanket.

beats.caption: unfolds a crinkly silver survival blanket

beats.text: Two blankets. One is military grade. One is from a 5K. The military one is yours.
And the canned beets?
Forty. Enough for us for a week. Or the office for a day.
Then it's for us.

lines: In a crisis, a man protects his tribe.
My tribe is very small. And very well-dressed. And I will not be naming her.

scenes.recap: Bob Vance rescues Phyllis with a truck with chains; the rest are stranded, and Oscar points out whose fault it is.

beats.text: Bob Vance, Vance Refrigeration. My truck has chains. Phyllis, let's go.
Bye, everyone! Stay warm!
Wait, can Bob take more people? Bob! Bob Vance! Ugh.
The state closed Route 6 at two. We'd be home if not for the snowman slides.
Or. Hear me out. This is the best thing that's ever happened to us.

lines: A sleepover. With my favorite people. I've only ever had one sleepover, in 1978.
Everyone left at nine. This time they can't.

scenes.recap: Jim and Pam make a vending-machine dinner and talk about what she wanted to be.

beats.caption: lays out two bags of pretzels, a Twix and a cup of soup like a dinner service

beats.text: Tonight's tasting menu. The chef recommends the Twix.
When I was ten I wanted to draw the pictures in children's books. Like, that was my whole plan.
What happened to the plan?
I don't know. Nothing happened to it. That's kind of what happened.
You're taking the class, though. That's something happening.

lines: Tonight is kind of... nice? Is that weird? We're trapped. In an office.

scenes.recap: Michael's 'Snow Games' flop, until Kevin produces a slow cooker of chili and dinner becomes a party.

beats.text: Welcome to the Snow Games! Event one: interpretive snow dance. Ryan, you're up.
No.
Event two: Who Can Be Quiet the Longest. Not you, Kelly.

beats.caption: sets a slow cooker on the table and lifts the lid

beats.text: I always keep a backup chili in my car. For emergencies. This is an emergency.
Best chili I've had since the commune.

scenes.recap: Late at night, Dwight and Angela share the survival blanket; Kevin wanders by for more chili and they spring apart.

beats.caption: shares a crinkly silver blanket with Angela, very close

beats.text: Is there more chili? Why is Angela in your blanket?
Body heat is a survival resource, Kevin. I'm saving her life. Clinically.
It's an emergency. Nothing about this is enjoyable.
Okay. Can I get in?
NO.

scenes.recap: Michael admits to Oscar that he stalled because his apartment is empty; Oscar softens and stays up playing cards with him.

beats.text: You did this on purpose, didn't you? The slides.
My place is very quiet in a storm, Oscar. It's quiet always. Storms make it louder.
...Do you play gin rummy?
I have never been asked that by someone who meant it.

lines: I'm still angry. He stranded eight people with a snowman PowerPoint.
He's also terrible at gin rummy. So I'm less angry.

scenes.recap: Near midnight, Jim and Pam watch the snow from reception; a quiet moment, until Roy calls to say the plow came through.

beats.text: It's so quiet. I've never heard the office quiet. It's like a different building.
I like it. I like the different building.
Roy? The plow came? You're coming now? Oh. Great. That's great.

lines: Roy got his truck out of the ditch. He's coming to get her. That's good. He's a good guy.
The plow guys are really fast. Like... really fast.

scenes.recap: In the morning the stranded crew wakes up in the conference room, and Michael has had the best night of his life.

beats.text: THE NEXT MORNING
Ryan slept next to me. That's basically a relationship milestone.
There were four chairs. I had no choice.

lines: Best night of my life. We ate chili. We played gin rummy. Ryan slept near people.
'Stuck in a room together.' Yeah. That's what a family is. Survey's wrong.

scenes.recap: Creed mentions he sleeps at the office most nights anyway.

beats.text: Creed, you seem very rested.
I sleep here most nights. The storm just meant company.
